lessons.title: Media habits
lessons.goal: Talk about how you keep up with the news and how much time you spend on screens.

tip.title: s'informer, l'actualité & ne … plus
tip.body: S'informer means to keep yourself informed; l'actualité (or les actualités, informally les infos) is the news in general, while le journal télévisé (le JT) is the TV news bulletin. Ne … plus means no longer: Je ne regarde plus la télé. In casual speech the ne is often dropped: Je regarde plus la télé — the s of plus stays silent here. Note the liaison in les_infos [lé-zin-fo]. In réseaux, the s between two vowels sounds like z [ré-zo], but there is no liaison in réseaux sociaux: [ré-zo so-sio].

lessons.title: Films and series
lessons.goal: Talk about what you're watching, recommend a series and avoid spoilers.

tip.title: VO, VF & recommending
tip.body: In France films and series are often dubbed: la VF (version française). If you want the original language with subtitles, ask for la VO or la VOST (version originale sous-titrée). To recommend something warmly, say Je te la conseille vivement (la = la série) or Je te le conseille (le = le film): the object pronoun goes before the verb. Pronunciation: série is [sé-ri] with two clear vowels, and in sous-titrée the s of sous is silent.

lessons.title: True or fake?
lessons.goal: Question a piece of news and explain how you check information.

tip.title: Talking about fake news
tip.body: French speakers say les fake news, but you will also hear les fausses informations, la désinformation and the official word une infox (info + intox). Fiable means reliable: une source fiable. Ça a l'air … means it looks/seems …: Ça a l'air faux. Pronunciation: in fiable the i glides into the a [fjabl], and in vérifier the final r is silent [vé-ri-fjé].

lessons.title: dont, ce qui & ce que
lessons.goal: Link ideas with dont, and say 'what' in the middle of a sentence with ce qui / ce que.

tip.title: dont = of which / about which; ce qui / ce que = what
tip.body: Dont replaces de + a noun after verbs and expressions built with de: parler de, avoir besoin de, se souvenir de, avoir peur de. C'est le film dont tout le monde parle (everyone talks about it → parler de). It also expresses whose: une journaliste dont j'admire le travail. English 'what' in the middle of a sentence is ce qui when it is the subject of the next verb (Ce qui m'intéresse…) and ce que when it is the object (Ce que je regarde…). Ce que becomes ce qu' before a vowel: ce qu'il dit. Pronunciation: dont is a nasal [dɔ̃]; before a vowel it is often linked: dont_il [dɔ̃-til].

story.title: A podcast about francophone music
story.intro: A Paris radio host interviews Émilie, a podcaster from Montréal who talks about francophone music.

lines.name: Animateur
lines.t: Bonjour à tous ! Aujourd'hui, notre invitée vient de Montréal. Bienvenue dans l'émission, Émilie !
lines.n: Hello everyone! Today our guest comes from Montréal. Welcome to the programme, Émilie!

lines.name: Émilie
lines.t: Bonjour ! Merci de m'inviter, je suis très contente d'être ici.
lines.n: Hello! Thanks for inviting me, I'm very happy to be here.

lines.name: Animateur
lines.t: Vous faites un podcast dont on parle beaucoup en ce moment. De quoi s'agit-il ?
lines.n: You make a podcast that people are talking about a lot at the moment. What is it about?

lines.name: Émilie
lines.t: C'est un podcast sur la musique francophone : des artistes du Québec, de Belgique, du Sénégal, de Suisse…
lines.n: It's a podcast about francophone music: artists from Québec, Belgium, Senegal, Switzerland…

lines.name: Animateur
lines.t: Et comment est-ce que vous travaillez ?
lines.n: And how do you work?

lines.name: Émilie
lines.t: On est deux. On enregistre chaque épisode à la maison, le dimanche, et on le publie le mercredi.
lines.n: There are two of us. We record every episode at home on Sundays, and we publish it on Wednesdays.

lines.name: Animateur
lines.t: Qu'est-ce qui vous plaît le plus dans ce travail ?
lines.n: What do you like most about this work?

lines.name: Émilie
lines.t: Ce que j'aime, c'est le contact avec le public. Les auditeurs nous écrivent souvent, même depuis l'Afrique de l'Ouest !
lines.n: What I love is the contact with the audience. Listeners often write to us, even from West Africa!

lines.name: Animateur
lines.t: Formidable. Merci d'être venue, Émilie, et bonne continuation !
lines.n: Wonderful. Thank you for coming, Émilie, and all the best!

lessons.title: My media life
lessons.goal: Talk for about 45 seconds about the media you use and recommend something.

culture.title: Francophone public media
culture.body: Each francophone country has its own public broadcaster: France Télévisions and Radio France in France, the RTBF in French-speaking Belgium, the RTS (Radio Télévision Suisse) in French-speaking Switzerland, and Radio-Canada, the French-language side of Canada's public broadcaster (ICI Radio-Canada). Internationally, TV5Monde is a joint francophone channel with partners from several countries, and RFI (Radio France Internationale) is widely listened to, especially in francophone Africa. Their websites and apps offer news, podcasts and programmes for learners — great free practice with different accents.
